how: A local server answered www.example.com and api.example.com, mapped to 127.0.0.1 with --host-resolver-rules, over HTTPS with HTTP/2, on ports of five digits, its certificate taken on trust by --ignore-certificate-errors alone, and kept the header block of every request as the bytes said it, connection by connection. Each scenario ran in a fresh profile: a URL opened from the command line, a page whose script called fetch() or navigated, each page naming an icon of its own so that no /favicon.ico came between. A run whose requests to one origin went on more than one connection, as Chrome does now and then with a spare one it opens beside a navigation's, was run again. Each field is said as it was written into HPACK (RFC 7541, section 6): indexed or a literal with or without indexing, its name from the static or the dynamic table by its index or written out, each string Huffman-coded or not, against the dynamic table the blocks before it on its connection left. The server's SETTINGS said a dynamic table of 4096 bytes, or of the scenario's table. The ports and the values are left out.
